entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Sorry for dragging you out here.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I was out here gathering intel, and I[n]noticed some patrons playing this...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I did a bit of research. Apparently it's a[n]pretty hardcore shooter game.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Do you normally play games like these?
All the time.
I'm not great at them.
Have you played any?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Oh, maybe you've played this one before?[n]I can only ask that you go easy on me.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Well, that should even the playing field.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I'm not much for video games myself,[n]so I guess I'm in the same boat.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Personally, no.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Well, I'm pretty sure I'll manage.

entries.speaker: Loud Young Man
entries.en: Damn, that's some accuracy. That guy[n]with the brown hair isn't wasting a[n]single shot.

entries.speaker: Gaudy Young Man
entries.en: Glasses isn't doing bad either, but he's[n]definitely losing ground...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Phew! My fingers are going to be sore[n]tomorrow. What a realistic game.
Are you used to gunplay?[clr 27]
You took that seriously, huh.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Ah, you noticed? Well, I'll need as much[n]practice as I can get if I'm going to take[n]you out.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: ...Only a joke.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I'm new to this, I'm afraid. Perhaps[n]we'll chalk it up to beginner's luck.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Ah, you noticed? Well, I'll need as much[n]practice as I can get if I'm going to take[n]you out.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Haha, only a joke.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: What, did I have that much of a[n]scary look on my face?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Still, this did feel a bit nostalgic for me.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I had a toy gun like this when I was[n]young, you know.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: All this reminded me of running around[n]the house with it, playing hero...
You wanted to be a hero?[clr 27]
Very interesting.
Hard to imagine.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I'm not totally certain, but thinking back,[n]I suppose I must have.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Is it? I don't think it's that unusual for[n]younger children.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: What kind of person do you imagine[n]me to be?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: But there are different kinds of heroes,[n]of course. Different stances they define[n]themselves by.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: For example, one may stick to the vision[n]of justice they believe in, even if others[n]deny it...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: While another may simply do as others[n]desire of them, seeking to be recognized[n]and gratified as a hero.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: So? Which of those two fits more with[n]your conception of a hero?
Sticking to your justice.
Doing what people want.
Neither, really.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Well, I had a feeling you'd say that.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: But if nobody else wants the justice[n]they fight for, isn't that just blind[n]self-righteousness?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: That's a surprise. I didn't think you'd[n]say that.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: But I suppose that's fair. After all, if this[n]"justice" isn't something people want,[n]then it's just empty self-righteousness.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: You believe there's a third option?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I suppose if you're fighting for a justice[n]nobody really wants, then it's just blind[n]self-righteousness in the end.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Ah, sorry. I suppose that was a strange[n]tangent... Pardon me.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Whenever I talk with you, I just can't help[n]delving into these abstract topics...
I feel like my bond with[n]Akechi is growing deeper...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Goodness, I worked up a sweat playing[n]that game. I must smell like the arcade[n]now...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I could use a shower. Why don't we[n]call it a day?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Well, see you again.
